name: The noun of time and place (ism al-zamān wa-l-makān)
definition: A noun on the pattern mafʿal or mafʿil for the time or place of an action: manṣar, 'the place or time of helping'.
body: From a three-letter verb it is mafʿal when the present has a or u in its middle (manṣar from yanṣuru) and mafʿil when it has i (majlis from yajlisu); from the augmented verbs it takes the form of the passive participle. The same pattern mafʿal also makes the 'maṣdar with mīm' (maṣdar mīmī), the verbal noun with a mīm before it: context tells which is meant.

examples.text: manṣar, the place or time of helping, in al-Amthila.
maḍrab, the place or time of striking.
